habitat: Mostly moist savanna, around villages, near cultivation and at forest fringes. Uncommon, like its host, in drier bushveld.
summary: A common resident. It has a whitish bill and reddish legs. The male has a grating song mixed with notes of the African Firefinch, which the female parasitises, and may bob while calling a harsh 'cha, cha'. Newman does not describe the body colour. The Kemp name Black Widowfinch and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Village Indigobird has a red bill and red legs.
Purple Indigobird has a whitish or pale pink bill and legs, and is more common in dry bushveld.

viewNotes.note: Whitish bill and reddish legs. The body colour is not described.
The male may bob in front of the female.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: A grating song mixed with notes of the African Firefinch. The male also calls a harsh 'cha, cha'. The grade A song is from near Fort Brown in the Eastern Cape. The filename is XC641307-Dusky Indigobird DHeights 27 Feb 2021.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The body colour is not described, so none is stored. The grade A recording is a song from the Eastern Cape. The Kemp name Black Widowfinch and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^11=2048 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 1024–4096.
